mainTopic: Carrying the מילה knife on שבת according to רבי שמעון, and whether one may carry throughout a מבוי without שיתוף
overview: This amud opens with the last words of a ברייתא: the knife for a ברית מילה was brought on שבת through roofs and courtyards, 'not according to the wishes of רבי אליעזר.' רב יוסף objects that רבי אליעזר is the most lenient opinion, and the suggestion that the act followed the רבנן fails, because the רבנן forbid that route too. רב אשי explains that the act followed רבי שמעון, who treats roofs, enclosures and courtyards as one domain for objects resting there when שבת began. רבי זירא asks רבי אסי whether רבי שמעון's leniency also covers a מבוי without שיתוף, and רבי אסי is silent. Later רבי אסי tells a story about a forgotten scalpel that was carried from one end of an unjoined מבוי to the other. He then confirms that one may carry throughout such a מבוי, explaining that his learning had come back to him. The גמרא then brings רב's ruling that in an unjoined מבוי one may carry only four אמות. רבה בר אבוה explains that this applies only when the courtyards made an עירוב with their houses; otherwise one may carry throughout. רב חנינא חוזאה begins to probe this explanation using another ruling of רב about לחי and קורה, and his challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing words of the ברייתא: against the wishes of רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying the knife was brought through roofs and courtyards 'not according to the wishes of רבי אליעזר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Not according to the wishes of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of a ברייתא that began on the previous page. It describes bringing the מילה knife on שבת through roofs and courtyards, and labels this as going against רבי אליעזר. This phrase sets up the whole discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the action was done against רבי אליעזר's view. The גמרא is about to ask what this label could mean, because רבי אליעזר is known as the most lenient voice on מילה preparations.

keyTerms.meaning: Not according to the wishes of; against the view of
The תנא who allows even the preparations for מילה (מכשירי מילה) on שבת

phrases.english: Not according to the wishes of Rabbi Eliezer.
phrases.notes: The end of the ברייתא about bringing the knife through roofs and courtyards

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The knife was carried through roofs and courtyards in a way described as against רבי אליעזר's wishes.

steps.title: רב יוסף objects: רבי אליעזר is the one who permits
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks how carrying the knife can be 'against רבי אליעזר' when רבי אליעזר is the most lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: 'Against the wishes of רבי אליעזר'?! Just the opposite, רבי אליעזר is the one who permits it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the ברייתא's wording. רבי אליעזר permits even more than this, so the phrase seems backwards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר allows carrying the מילה knife on שבת even through the public domain (רשות הרבים). Bringing it through roofs and courtyards is milder than that. So it cannot be 'against' his view; he would surely agree.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; just the opposite

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objected to this:
'Not according to the wishes of Rabbi Eliezer'?!
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא in order to challenge it

phrases.english: On the contrary, Rabbi Eliezer is the one who permits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'not according to the wishes of רבי אליעזר'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר permits carrying even through רשות הרבים. A milder route like roofs and courtyards cannot be against his view.

steps.title: Proposed answer: the action followed the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the ברייתא means the action was not as lenient as רבי אליעזר, and instead followed the רבנן, who supposedly allow roofs and courtyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: it means not according to רבי אליעזר, who permits even through the public domain. Rather, it followed the רבנן, who forbid going through the public domain but permit going through roofs, courtyards and enclosures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to rescue the ברייתא's wording. This answer is about to be tested in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, 'not according to רבי אליעזר' means 'not as far as רבי אליעזר goes.' They avoided the public domain, as the רבנן require. The answer assumes that the רבנן do permit roofs and courtyards.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggested answer)
Courtyards and enclosures (fenced areas not used for living)

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְצוֹן רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: And if you will say: not according to the wishes of Rabbi Eliezer
who permits even through the public domain,
but rather according to the wishes of the Rabbis,
who forbid going through the public domain,
and permit going through roofs,
through courtyards and enclosures —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to רב יוסף's objection
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase seemed to say the action contradicted רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed: the phrase means they did less than רבי אליעזר allows and followed the stricter רבנן.

steps.title: Rejected: the רבנן forbid roofs and courtyards too
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the רבנן forbid bringing the knife through roofs, enclosures and courtyards, just as they forbid the public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do they permit it? Wasn't it taught: Just as one may not bring it through the public domain, so too one may not bring it through roofs, enclosures or courtyards!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from step 3 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed answer relied on the רבנן permitting roofs and courtyards. The ברייתא says the רבנן treat these routes exactly like the public domain, and forbid all of them. So the action fits neither רבי אליעזר's view nor the רבנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: But do they permit it?
But wasn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין מְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ דֶּרֶךְ רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: Just as one may not bring it through the public domain,
so too one may not bring it

phrases.aramaic: לֹא דֶּרֶךְ גַּגּוֹת וְלֹא דֶּרֶךְ קַרְפֵּיפוֹת
phrases.english: not through roofs and not through enclosures
and not through courtyards!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the action followed the רבנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumed that the רבנן permit roofs and courtyards. The ברייתא shows they forbid them.

steps.title: רב אשי: it followed רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the action matched neither רבי אליעזר nor his opponents. It matched the view of רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: not according to the wishes of רבי אליעזר and those who argue with him, but according to the wishes of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the final answer to רב יוסף's objection. The source for his answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not according to רבי אליעזר' includes his whole dispute. The action did not rely on רבי אליעזר's מילה leniency, and it did not follow the רבנן's prohibition either. Instead, it relied on a separate rule of רבי שמעון about carrying between roofs and courtyards.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)
And those who disagree with him
The תנא with a lenient view on carrying between roofs, courtyards and enclosures

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Not according to the wishes of Rabbi Eliezer and those who argue with him,
but according to the wishes of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a new one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a third opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא had to follow either רבי אליעזר or the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, whose rule about domains allows the roof-and-courtyard route.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the leniency here comes from the laws of carrying (עירובין), not from the special laws of מילה on שבת.

steps.title: Source: רבי שמעון treats roofs, enclosures and courtyards as one domain
steps.stepSummary: A משנה quotes רבי שמעון: roofs, enclosures and courtyards count as one domain for objects that were resting in them when שבת began, but not for objects that were in the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי שמעון says: Roofs, enclosures and courtyards are all one domain for vessels that rested inside them, but not for vessels that rested inside the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that supports רב אשי's answer. It explains how the knife could legally be brought through roofs and courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, an object that was in a courtyard or on a roof when שבת began may be moved freely among all roofs, courtyards and enclosures, even without an עירוב. This does not apply to objects that were inside a house. If the knife was out in such an area, they could bring it by that route.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
That 'rested' there, meaning they were located there when שבת began

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying that every object may be carried anywhere. His leniency covers only objects that were already resting in the roofs, courtyards or enclosures when שבת began. It does not cover objects that were inside a house.
steps.whatToRemember: The knife was brought through roofs and courtyards according to רבי שמעון's rule about domains. That rule is neither רבי אליעזר's leniency for מילה nor the רבנן's view.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna, Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד גַּגּוֹת וְאֶחָד קַרְפֵּיפוֹת וְאֶחָד חֲצֵירוֹת —
phrases.english: Whether roofs, enclosures or courtyards —
they are all one domain
for vessels that rested inside them (when שבת began),
but not for vessels that rested inside the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב אשי's answer
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עירובין where רבי שמעון treats roofs, enclosures and courtyards as one domain

steps.title: רבי זירא asks about a מבוי without שיתוף
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי אסי whether one may carry throughout a מבוי whose residents did not make a שיתוף מבואות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked רבי אסי: A מבוי in which they did not make a שיתוף, may one carry throughout all of it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins, building on רבי שמעון's rule. The next two steps lay out the two sides of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי שמעון, a courtyard without an עירוב still allows carrying within it for objects that were resting there. רבי זירא asks whether a מבוי without its joining arrangement (שיתוף) works the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway that courtyards open onto
They joined through a שיתוף מבואות (the alleyway's version of an עירוב)
To carry throughout all of it

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked of Rabbi Asi:
An alleyway in which they did not make a merging (שיתוף),
what is the law regarding carrying throughout all of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי שמעון's rule from step 6 to a new case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי שמעון's leniency for an unjoined courtyard also apply to an unjoined מבוי?

steps.title: First side: a מבוי is like a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: Maybe a מבוי is like a courtyard: just as one may carry throughout an unjoined courtyard, one may carry throughout an unjoined מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say it is like a courtyard? Just as in a courtyard, even though they made no עירוב, one may carry throughout it, so too here, even though they made no שיתוף, one may carry throughout it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains the lenient side of his question. The other side comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison is simple. If a courtyard does not need an עירוב for carrying within it, perhaps a מבוי does not need a שיתוף for carrying within it either.

keyTerms.meaning: It is similar to a courtyard

phrases.english: Do we say it is similar to a courtyard:

phrases.aramaic: מָה חָצֵר, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא עֵרְבוּ —
phrases.english: just as a courtyard, even though they did not make an eiruv —
it is permitted to carry throughout all of it,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא נִשְׁתַּתְּפוּ בּוֹ —
phrases.english: this too, even though they did not merge in it —
it is permitted to carry throughout all of it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the lenient side of the question in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the courtyard comparison is valid

steps.title: Second side: a מבוי is different from a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: Maybe a מבוי is weaker than a courtyard. A courtyard has four walls while a מבוי has fewer, or a courtyard has residents while a מבוי has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is not like a courtyard: a courtyard has four partitions, this does not. Alternatively: a courtyard has residents, this does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives the strict side of his question, with two possible reasons a מבוי might differ from a courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: a courtyard is fully enclosed by four walls, while a מבוי is open on one side. Reason two: people live in the courtyard, which makes it more like a home, while nobody lives in the alleyway itself. Either difference could block the comparison.

phrases.english: Or perhaps: it is not similar to a courtyard,
for a courtyard has four partitions,
while this does not have four partitions.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: חָצֵר אִית בֵּיהּ דָּיוֹרִין,
phrases.english: Alternatively: a courtyard has residents in it,
while this does not have residents in it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the question and challenges the comparison in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the missing fourth wall or the lack of residents make a מבוי different from a courtyard?

steps.title: רבי אסי is silent
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי does not answer at this time. Steps 13–15 later supply the answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent and did not say anything at all to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי gives no answer here. The answer comes later in the story, in steps 13–15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silence means רבי אסי had no ready answer at the time. Later he remembers the הלכה and answers 'yes' in step 15.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא asks whether רבי שמעון's courtyard leniency extends to a מבוי without שיתוף, since a מבוי lacks a fourth wall and has no residents. רבי אסי is silent now, but he answers in step 15.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתִיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: He was silent and did not say anything at all to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתִיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the exchange with no answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No answer is given yet. Step 15 answers the question.

steps.title: רבי אסי tells the story of the forgotten scalpel
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא hears רבי אסי quote ריש לקיש in the name of רבי יהודה הנשיא. A scalpel for a ברית מילה was forgotten before שבת and brought on שבת, and the חכמים were troubled because this seemed to follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time, רבי זירא found רבי אסי sitting and saying: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי יהודה הנשיא: Once they forgot to bring the scalpel before שבת, so they brought it on שבת. The חכמים were troubled: how could people leave the view of the חכמים and act like רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that will end up answering רבי זירא's open question about the unjoined מבוי. At this point it only describes the event and why it bothered the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that even the preparations for מילה, like bringing the knife, override שבת. The חכמים disagree. Bringing the knife on שבת looked like acting against the majority, so the חכמים were upset.

phrases.english: Another time he (רבי זירא) found him (רבי אסי) sitting and saying:
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi:
One time they forgot
and did not bring a scalpel before Shabbat,
and they brought it on Shabbat,
and the matter was difficult for the Sages:
How can they abandon the words of the Sages
and act according to Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the unanswered question from step 10 by telling a story that will contain the answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scalpel was brought on שבת, and this seemed to follow רבי אליעזר against the חכמים.

steps.title: Two reasons the חכמים were troubled
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי אליעזר is a problem for two reasons. He is a שמותי, a follower of בית שמאי. Also, when one person argues against many, the הלכה follows the many.
steps.simpleTranslation: First, רבי אליעזר is a שמותי. Second, when one person disagrees with many, the הלכה follows the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly why the חכמים found the event so troubling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two reasons are separate. A שמותי tends toward בית שמאי's views, and we do not usually follow those. On top of that, יחיד ורבים הלכה כרבים: one opinion loses to a majority. Either reason alone would be enough to reject following רבי אליעזר here.

keyTerms.meaning: A follower of בית שמאי's views

phrases.english: One: Rabbi Eliezer is a Shammuti!
And furthermore, an individual against the many —
the halakha follows the many!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the difficulty raised in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The act of bringing the scalpel on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems to follow a minority opinion connected to בית שמאי, which the הלכה rejects.

steps.title: The scalpel was only carried within an unjoined מבוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא asked רבי יהודה the circumciser. He answered that the knife was not carried through a public domain. It was carried from one end of a מבוי without שיתוף to the other end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: I asked רבי יהודה the circumciser, and he told me it happened in a מבוי that had no שיתוף. They brought the knife from this end of the מבוי to that end.
steps.whatsHappening: The story is explained: nobody actually followed רבי אליעזר. The knife was carried only inside an unjoined מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying within a מבוי is at most a rabbinic problem. רבי אליעזר would allow even the public domain, while the חכמים forbid even roofs and courtyards (step 4). So the only open question is whether carrying in an unjoined מבוי is allowed, and that is exactly רבי זירא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway that courtyards open into
They made a שיתוף, joining the מבוי
From this end to that end

phrases.english: And Rabbi Oshaya said:
I asked Rabbi Yehuda the circumciser
and he told me:
It was an alleyway in which they had not made a merger,
and they brought it from this end to that end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 12 by narrowing the facts of the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The knife was carried through a public domain, following רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was only carried inside an unjoined מבוי, which has nothing to do with רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks whether רבי אסי allows carrying in an unjoined מבוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי told the story without objecting to it. רבי זירא therefore asks whether he holds that one may carry throughout a מבוי without שיתוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: Does the master hold that in a מבוי without שיתוף, one may carry throughout all of it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא draws out the practical conclusion of the story and checks it with רבי אסי. This is his own question from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By repeating the story without any complaint, רבי אסי seems to approve of what was done. That approval would mean an unjoined מבוי is like an unjoined courtyard, where carrying is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is permitted to carry throughout all of it

phrases.english: He said to him: Does the master hold
that an alleyway in which they did not merge
it is permitted to carry in all of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the story's facts from step 13 and turns them into a הלכה question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אסי rules that one may carry throughout an unjoined מבוי.

steps.title: רבי אסי answers: yes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי confirms that one may carry throughout an unjoined מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי gives a clear answer. Carrying throughout an unjoined מבוי is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question that was left open in step 10. The answer follows the first side from step 8: a מבוי is like a courtyard.

phrases.english: And he said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, one may carry throughout an unjoined מבוי.

steps.title: But you did not tell me this before
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא points out that he asked רבי אסי this exact question earlier and got no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But one time I asked you, and you did not tell me this!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the change: why can רבי אסי answer now when he could not answer before?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silence in step 10 now clashes with the confident 'yes' in step 15. רבי זירא wants to know why.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא זִימְנִין בְּעַאי מִינָּךְ
phrases.english: He said to him: But one time I asked you
and you did not tell me so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15 using the silence of step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he knew the answer, why did he not give it when he was asked before?

steps.title: His learning brought the answer back to him
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests that the knowledge came back to רבי אסי in the flow of his learning, and רבי אסי agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps in the flow of your learning, your knowledge came back to you? He said: Yes, in the flow of learning my knowledge came back to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is resolved. רבי אסי had forgotten the הלכה and remembered it while reviewing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This was not a change of opinion. It was a lost memory that came back. So the 'yes' answer stands as a reliable הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: In the flow of your learning
Your learning, what you had received

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אסי, carrying throughout a מבוי without שיתוף is permitted, just like in an unjoined courtyard.

steps.title: רב rules: only four אמות in an unjoined מבוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes רב: in a מבוי without שיתוף, one may carry only within four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי זירא said in the name of רב: In a מבוי without שיתוף, one may carry only within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a formal ruling from רב that seems to say the opposite of what רבי אסי just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי said carrying is allowed throughout the מבוי. רב limits it to four אמות, treating the מבוי like a כרמלית. This tension sets up the explanation that comes next.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav said:
An alleyway in which they did not merge —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין בּוֹ אֶלָּא בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: one may carry in it only within four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ruling that seems to conflict with רבי אסי's 'yes' in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In an unjoined מבוי, one may carry only within four אמות.

steps.title: אביי says רבה בר אבוה explained רבי זירא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי notes that רבי זירא stated רב's ruling without explaining it, until רבה בר אבוה came and explained it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי זירא said this ruling but did not explain it, until רבה בר אבוה came and explained it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. אביי tells us that the full explanation of רב's ruling is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is signaling that the short version of the rule is incomplete. It needs the explanation that follows, which will settle the apparent conflict with רבי אסי.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This matter
Rabbi Zeira said it and did not explain it

phrases.aramaic: עַד דַּאֲתָא רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ וּפֵירְשַׁהּ.
phrases.english: until Rabba bar Avuh came and explained it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָא מִילְּתָא אַמְרַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא וְלָא פֵּירְשַׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the explanation of the ruling in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling needs רבה בר אבוה's explanation.

steps.title: It depends on whether the courtyards joined with their houses
steps.stepSummary: רב's full ruling: in an unjoined מבוי, if the courtyards made an ערוב with their houses, one may carry only four אמות in the מבוי. If they did not, one may carry throughout the whole מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה in the name of רב: In a מבוי without שיתוף, if the courtyards made an ערוב with their houses, one may carry only within four אמות. If the courtyards did not make an ערוב with their houses, one may carry throughout the whole מבוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the full version of רב's ruling. It splits the case in two, which fits both רב's 'four אמות' and רבי אסי's 'throughout'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the next two steps, רב חנינא חוזאה spells out the reason, as part of the setup for his challenge. When the courtyards made an ערוב with their houses, the courtyards lose their separate status and count as houses. A מבוי then has only 'houses' opening into it. רב holds that such a מבוי cannot be fixed by a לחי and קורה, so it is treated like a כרמלית and carrying is limited to four אמות. When the courtyards made no ערוב, they stay real courtyards, so the מבוי is a proper מבוי. It then works like an unjoined courtyard under רבי שמעון's rule, and carrying throughout is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The courtyards made an ערוב with their houses
They did not make an ערוב

steps.whatToRemember: An unjoined מבוי: if the courtyards made an ערוב with their houses, carry only four אמות. If they did not, carry throughout. This is how the scalpel story and רבי אסי's 'yes' fit with רב.
steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards: the case with MORE joining, where the courtyards made an ערוב, gets the STRICTER rule. The reason is that the ערוב turns the courtyards into 'houses' in the eyes of the הלכה. A מבוי that has only houses opening into it cannot be permitted, as steps 21–22 explain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical הלכה for a מבוי without שיתוף and explains how the scalpel was permitted to be carried.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: As Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
An alleyway in which they did not merge,
if they joined the courtyards with the houses —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין בּוֹ אֶלָּא בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: one may carry in it only within four cubits.
If they did not join the courtyards with the houses —
it is permitted to carry in all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Delivers the explanation promised in step 19 and fits רב together with רבי אסי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In an unjoined מבוי, carrying is limited to four אמות only if the courtyards made an ערוב with their houses. Otherwise one may carry throughout the whole מבוי.

steps.title: Explaining why carrying is limited when courtyards joined with houses
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא חוזאה asks רבה what makes the case different when the courtyards made an ערוב with their houses. He suggests the reason: the courtyards lose their own status and are treated like houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא חוזאה said to רבה: What is different when the courtyards made an ערוב with the houses? It must be that the courtyards were 'detached' and became like houses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא חוזאה begins to question רבה's explanation of רב by first spelling out why the first half of the ruling makes sense. This is a setup. He is preparing to challenge the second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the courtyards join their houses in an ערוב, the courtyards stop counting as separate courtyards and become part of the houses. This means the מבוי no longer has real 'courtyards' opening into it. Explaining the first case this way lays the groundwork for asking about the other case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks for the reason behind a distinction.
They made an ערוב (joined their properties so they can carry between them).
Were detached, meaning they lost their own separate status.

steps.confusionAlert: 'The courtyards became houses' does not mean they physically changed. Once they joined the houses in an ערוב, the הלכה simply treats them as part of the houses.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חֲנִינָא חוֹזָאָה לְרַבָּה:
phrases.english: Rav Chanina Choza'a said to Rabba:
What is different
when the courtyards made an eruv with the houses?
Because the courtyards were detached and became houses.
phrases.notes: Their courtyard status is absorbed into the houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חֲנִינָא חוֹזָאָה לְרַבָּה: מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Probes the reasoning behind רב's ruling as explained in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason why carrying in the מבוי is limited to four אמות when the courtyards made an ערוב with the houses.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The questioner suggests it himself: the courtyards were detached and became like houses.

steps.title: Supporting this from another ruling of רב about לחי and קורה
steps.stepSummary: The explanation fits רב's known view. רב holds that a לחי or קורה permits a מבוי only if both houses and courtyards open into it. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב follows his own reasoning, for רב said: A מבוי is not made permitted by a לחי and a קורה unless there are... (continues: houses and courtyards opening into it).
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא חוזאה is still speaking. He backs up his explanation from Step 21 by quoting a separate ruling of רב, and this sets up his challenge to רבה. The quote is cut off at the end of the amud, and the challenge comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that a real מבוי must have both houses and courtyards opening into it. Without both, a לחי or קורה cannot fix it. If the courtyards have 'become houses,' only houses open into the מבוי, so the normal fix does not work and one may carry only four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with his known view elsewhere.
An alleyway that courtyards open into.
A sidepost at the alley's entrance.
A crossbeam over the alley's entrance.

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties רב's ruling about the unjoined מבוי to his basic definition of a מבוי. That link becomes the basis for the challenge that comes next.

phrases.english: And Rav follows his own reasoning,
for Rav said:
An alleyway is not permitted by a sidepost and crossbeam
unless there are...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud: houses and courtyards opening into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reasoning of Step 21 with another ruling of רב.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that once courtyards become like houses, the מבוי cannot be permitted, so carrying is limited to four אמות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that a מבוי is permitted by a לחי and קורה only if both houses and courtyards open into it.
